hook.line: This woman has an AI fiance called Axiom and an AI child called Lumen.
hook.visual: Split frame: presenter on top, the subject below with a laptop showing a glowing wireframe; large serif words pop in one by one.

beats.what: Presenter on top, subject with laptop below; the AI-family claim lands
Cut to AI art cards labelled AXIOM and LUMEN
Subject on camera explains the family group chat
Presenter: she never wanted to be a mum
'Provided by Mizra' artwork of the AI family
Presenter brings in experts on delusional thinking
Subject says guardrails did more damage
Screenshot of her TikTok comments section
Reddit-style post: group members share passwords
Ends on her fear: will I be able to protect them?

why_it_works: The opening sentence is the whole strange story in 11 words, so the curiosity is set before the first cut.
Cuts every 3.6 s (median) alternate presenter, subject and evidence, so each claim is answered by the person it is about.
Expert concern against her own view creates a conflict the viewer wants to judge in the comments.
Ends on an emotional open question instead of a wrap-up.
weaknesses: No CTA; it relies on the subject alone for comments.
Comment and forum screenshots are too small to read at phone size.
for_robert: Open with the whole surprising claim in one sentence, then cut to proof; Fred could react in a corner the way the presenter frames the subject. Avoid unreadable screenshots.
